main_body: Flat dark-green ground patch (4x3 tiles) with a repeating 16px pattern of moss/grass flecks, small yellow and red dots. It is terrain, not a standing object.
top_band: none (flat ground texture; the scan shows only a repeating 16-row pattern of L=65 base with small speckle rows)
evidence: Terrain ground patch, so the 3/4 standing-object contract does not apply. There is no standing body, no top/front split, and no isometric side face. The column scan shows only a repeating tile pattern of speckles on a uniform base, which is normal for seamless ground. Treated as a valid terrain tile.

style.evidence: Candidate has 12 distinct colours and a median of 12 per tile. That is above the paving reference (7) but far below the grass reference (26 per tile, 80 colours). The ground is a single dark olive base with sparse light-green and dark specks plus isolated yellow and red dots. The base is one flat colour with a regular grid-like speckle repeat, so it reads as a tiled stamp rather than grass shaded clump by clump. Shading ramp is about 4 steps (base, dark, light, highlight) against about 6 in the grass reference. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no big flat areas, and the dark edge pixels are not neutral (0%), so there is no sticker outline. Yet the texture is thin and mechanical, with visibly identical repeated motifs and no clump structure, and it is clearly less rich than the grass reference. Standing next to the grass, it would look thinner and flatter.
